content: The following individuals and groups contributed to the development of tuberculosis (TB) care guidelines and related research: 1. Contributors from Various Organizations: R. Cravo Neto and Thomas Gradel from Unitaid, Switzerland. Charlotte Colvin from USAID, United States. Anne Detjen from UNICEF, United States. Brian Kaiser from the Stop TB Partnership Global Drug Facility, Switzerland. Michael McCaul and Celeste Naude from Stellenbosch University, South Africa. Lawrence Mbuagbaw from St. Joseph’s Healthcare, Canada. Oxana Rucsineanu from the TB Community Advisory Board. Anna Scardigli from the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria, Switzerland. Cherise Scott from Unitaid, Switzerland. 2. External Review Group: Martina Casenghi from the Elizabeth Glaser Pediatric AIDS Foundation, Switzerland. Anthony Enimil from Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital, Ghana. Malgorzata Grzemska, a former WHO staff member from Poland. Catherine Hewison from Médecins Sans Frontières, France. Devan Jaganath from the University of California, San Francisco, United States. Kobto Ghislain Koura from the International Union Against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease, France. Celia Martínez de Cuellar from Hospital de Clínicas, Universidad Nacional de Asunción, Paraguay. Ya Diul Mukadi from USAID, United States. Rahab Mwaniki from the Kenya AIDS NGOs Consortium (KANCO), Kenya. Marc Nicol from the University of Western Australia, Australia. Elizabeth Maleche Obimbo from the University of Nairobi, Kenya. Peter Owiti from the Wote Youth Development Project, Kenya. Nyan Win Phyo from the Civil Society Taskforce and World Vision, Thailand. Ramatoulaye Sall, an independent consultant from Senegal. Rina Triasih from Universitas Gadjah Mada, Indonesia. Eric Wobudeya from Mulago National Referral Hospital and Makerere University–Johns Hopkins University Research Collaboration, Uganda. 3. Evidence Reviewers: Yael Hirsch-Moverman from Columbia University, United States. Hamidah Hussain from Interactive Research and Development (IRD) Global, Singapore. Daria Szkwarcko from Brown University, United States. Courtney Yuen from Harvard Medical School, United States. These reviewers conducted evidence reviews for PICO Question 6, focusing on models of care for TB case detection and prevention in high TB burden settings. 4. WHO Steering Group: Members included Annabel Baddeley, Lice Gonzalez Angulo, Ernesto Jaramillo, Avinash Kanchar, and Charalambos Sismanidis from the WHO Global Tuberculosis Programme. Additional contributors from other WHO departments included Martina Penazzato, Bernadette Cappello, Lorenzo Moja, Marie Valentin, Corinne Simone Collette Merle, Valentina Baltag, Wilson Milton Were, Lina Mahy, Chiara Servili, Sarah Rylance, and others from regional WHO offices and specialized programs. 5. Guideline Development Group (GDG) for Drug-Resistant TB Treatment (2011): Members included Jaime Bayona (Socios En Salud, Peru), José A. Caminero (University General Hospital of Gran Canaria, Spain), Charles L. Daley (National Jewish Health, United States), Agnes Gebhard (Royal Dutch Tuberculosis Foundation, Netherlands), Myriam Henkens (Médecins Sans Frontières, France), and others with expertise in clinical practice, public health, epidemiology, and program management. 6. Evidence Review Teams: Teams included Chunling Lu, Carole D. Mitnick, and Richard A. White from Harvard Medical School and Harvard School of Public Health, United States. Additional contributors included Gail Kennedy, George Rutherford, and Karen Steingart from the University of California, San Francisco, and Matthew Arentz, David Horne, Patricia Pavlinac, and Judd L. Watson from the University of Washington, United States. 7. Consultants: Patricia Whyte from Griffith University, Australia, contributed to guideline development. 8. PICO Questions and Models of Care: The guidelines addressed interventions to promote adherence to TB treatment, including medication monitors, SMS or telephone reminders, and social support (educational, psychological, or material). They also explored models of care for drug-resistant TB, comparing ambulatory therapy with inpatient treatment and decentralized versus centralized care. Specific focus was given to children and adolescents, evaluating family-centered, integrated services versus standard care to improve TB case detection and prevention. 9. Web Annexes: Supporting materials included GRADE evidence profiles, evidence-to-decision tables, and other resources to inform decision-making. This comprehensive effort involved experts from diverse fields and organizations worldwide, ensuring a robust and evidence-based approach to TB care and prevention.
